data.gender_notes: Munna is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who protects, a source of joy and peace. The name Munna carries the meaning “Protector” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Pashto. Parents who choose Munna usually hope their child will grow to embody protector and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Munna belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Protector.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Munna total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Munna is of Arabic origin and has its roots deeply embedded in Islamic culture. It is a beautiful name that has been given to children not only due to its pleasant sound but also due to the meaning it holds. Munna is a name that conveys the significance of protection and caring, essential aspects of Islamic values. In a society where the concept of family, caring and protection is cherished, this name holds immense cultural importance.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Munna lies in its connotation of being a source of joy and peace. In Islam, it is believed that every person is a reflection of Allah, and hence, protecting and caring for them is a means of demonstrating love and reverence for the Creator. The name Munna symbolizes this commitment towards safeguarding the happiness and well-being of those around us, as well as ourselves, in a world that can often be challenging and unforgiving. The name is a constant reminder of the important role we play in the lives of those we love, and the religious duty to be a source of solace and tranquility in their times of need.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Protector" symbolizes The one who protects, a source of joy and peace. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Munna serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of protector.
